Letters home: truth vs lies

Today we will:

  1. play Two truths and a lie
  2. check Stanley's letter: true, half-true or a lie?
  3. learn how to make bad news sound nice
  4. write Stanley's next letter home, with a hidden truth

SAY ITno writingStanley's first letter (chapter 9)

True, half-true or a lie?

Dear Mom,

Today was my first day at camp, and I've already made some friends. We've been out on the lake all day, so I'm pretty tired. Once I pass the swimming test, I'll get to learn how to water-ski...

"my first day at camp"HALF-TRUE: it's really a "juvenile correctional facility".
"I've already made some friends"HALF-TRUE: Armpit threw him to the ground!
"out on the lake all day"HALF-TRUE: the lake is dry. He was digging a hole.
"I'm pretty tired"TRUE: blisters, sunburn, aching muscles.
"learn how to water-ski"LIE: there is no water to ski on.
Why does he lie? He doesn't want his mother to worry. We know the truth; she doesn't.
SAY ITmatch them, no writingThe trick: make the truth sound nice

  1. 1I dig a hole 5 feet deep every single day.
  2. 2The Warden owns the only shade.
  3. 3Mr Sir says I'll be thirsty for 18 months.
  4. 4My cot used to belong to a boy called Barf Bag.
  5. 5The Warden makes us dig the dirt twice.
  • AThe counselors teach us not to waste water.
  • BI get lots of exercise outdoors.
  • CWe are very careful with our work.
  • DThe camp director has a lovely hammock.
  • EI have my own bed, and it's already broken in!
1-B   2-D   3-A   4-E   5-CYour turn: make one up for "Armpit threw me to the ground."
WATCHno writing yetA model letter

Camp Green Lake, Texas

Dear Mom,

I'm having a busy week! I get lots of exercise outdoors, and my arms are getting really strong. The other boys gave me a nickname, Caveman, so I think they like me.

On Tuesday I found a fossil of a fish. Can you believe fish lived here once? The camp director came to visit us. She is very interested in everything we find, so we all worked extra hard.

Don't worry, I'm drinking lots of water, when they let us.

Love, Stanley

  • nice version a half-truth
  • real event from chapters 9-15
  • hidden truth a clue for a careful reader

Layout: where he is · Dear Mom, · 2-3 short paragraphs · Love, Stanley

Can you spot the hidden truth? What does it tell his mother, if she reads carefully?

Checklist

  • where he is + Dear Mom + Love, Stanley
  • 3 real events from the book
  • at least 2 nice versions (half-truths)
  • 1 hidden truth
  • written as Stanley ("I")
Halfway check at 7 minutes: you should be on paragraph 2. Extension (early finishers): write Mom's reply. Has she noticed the hidden truth?
SAY ITswap and talk, no writingSpot the hidden truth

Be Stanley's mother

  1. Swap notebooks with your partner.
  2. Read their letter as if you were Stanley's mother.
  3. Find the hidden truth. Say what it really means.
  4. Find one nice version. Say what really happened.

Volunteers read a letter aloud. The class guesses the hidden truth.
